finding: Confirmed per-actor duplication of immutable static enemy surface buffers; a substantial source of late-wave memory pressure. The physical iPad/Safari black-render symptom has not been reproduced on this desktop.
fix: Share immutable compatible static merged geometry only within the same decoded enemy source; retain private moving fields, transforms and materials. Reference-count static surfaces through previews, living figures and corpses, and release only after the final borrower leaves.

measurements.category: CPU typed-array byte lengths of runtime merged static geometry; excludes original decoded GLB resources, moving geometry, scene textures, other game assets and renderer overhead. Shared BufferGeometry also enables Three.js to share its corresponding WebGL geometry buffers.

coverage: All 54 enemy movement controllers retain private moving fields
Exact byte parity for all 92 approved enemy/champion moving surfaces
Actual host_44/host_45 shared vs independently merged full-geometry, normals, matrices and material identity parity
Shared geometry retained when one actor or corpse is disposed; final borrower disposes once
Different decoded source, transform or material cannot share incompatible geometry
29 actual wave44 figures retain 7 static merged buffers and cleanup returns all sharing counters to zero
Existing model-loader, geometric-resource ownership and WebGL diagnostic tests

limitations: Physical iPad/Safari not available for validation
The exact driver-level reason for black output is not proven
The measured saving is the runtime merged static geometry category, not total browser or GPU memory or a measured frame-rate claim
